extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/arithmetic-geometry familiar with Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of definitions, properties, and reconstruction algorithms for D-/F-prime-strips, NF-bridges, (2)-bridges, D-(2)-Hodge theatres, label-classes-of-cusps, and related group-theoretic structures appearing in IUT (inter-universal Teichmüller theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: LabCusp(yDv): label classes of cusps
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in V, a label class of cusps of yDv is the set of cusps of yDv lying over a single non-zero cusp of yD_v (each label class consists of two cusps). LabCusp(yDv) denotes the set of label classes and has a natural F_l-torsor structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A canonical element y^(17)_v in LabCusp(yDv) can be algorithmically reconstructed from the initial (2)-data (via cited Lemmas for different v-types). LabCusp(yDv) is used throughout to synchronise cusp-labellings and to compare components across v in V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical bijections among LabCusp across prime-strips (Prop.10.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a D-prime-strip yD = {yDv}_{v in V}, for any v,w in V there exist unique bijections LabCusp(yDv) -> LabCusp(yDw) compatible with the F_l-torsor structures and sending canonical elements to canonical elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By these identifications one may write a global LabCusp(yD) with a canonical element coming from the local y^(17)_v's; these bijections are foundational to transporting cusp-label information across components of a prime-strip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model D-NF-Bridge (Definition 10.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the subgroup Aut^(15)(C_K) <= Aut(C_K) = Out((pi_1)_{CK}) = Aut(D~) consisting of elements fixing a specified cusp, and describes the natural homomorphism Out((pi_1)_{CK}) -> Aut((pi_1)^ab_X[Fl]) = GL2(Fl)/{±1}. Introduces identifications of images as subgroups (e.g. containing Borel, images of GF_mod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces notation V_un, VBor and explains that VBor is the F_l-orbit of V_un. These group-theoretic identifications permit reconstruction of D-objects and connect automorphism subgroups with GL2(Fl)/{±1} images; key for defining model bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model D-(2)-Bridge and evaluation sections (Definition 10.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in V_bad there is a natural bijection between the set of cusps of C_v and jFlj; labels (2 jFlj) on collections of cusps of X_v and X are introduced. There exists a unique torsion point of order 2 (denoted (cid:22)(cid:0)) whose closure intersects same irreducible component of special fiber as cusp labelled 0; translating cusps by this torsion point yields evaluation points/sections labelled by j in jFlj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation points of X_v labelled by j have algebraic properties (rationality over K_v under certain conditions) and their images under coverings are constrained; arithmetic and group-theoretic reconstruction (elliptic cuspidalisation, Lemmas) allow recovery of evaluation sections from (an isomorph of) the relevant outer action object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-(or D-)NF-bridge (Definition 10.18 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(or D-)NF-bridge is a poly-morphism y^(30)NF_> : yDJ -> yD~ where yD~ is a category equivalent to the model global object D~, and yDJ is a capsule of D-prime-strips indexed by a finite set J, such that there exist isomorphisms D~ ≃ yD~ and D^> ≃ yD^>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphisms of D-NF-bridges are given by conjugation by capsule-full poly-isomorphisms and Aut^(15)(D~)-orbits; compositions defined in the evident manner. Base-bridges appear as building blocks for higher structures (Hodge theatres).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-(or D-)(2)-bridge (Definition 10.18 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(or D-)(2)-bridge is a poly-morphism y^(30)(2)_> : yDJ -> yD^> where yD^> is a D-prime-strip and yDJ a capsule of D-prime-strips indexed by finite J, with required isomorphisms to model objects and compatible full-poly isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphisms and compositions are defined by capsule-full poly-isomorphisms together with full-poly isomorphisms of the D-prime-strips; it is emphasised this structure is not necessarily a poly-isomorphism globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-(or D-)(2)-Hodge theatre (Definition 10.18 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(or D-)(2)-Hodge theatre is a triple (yD~, y^(30)NF_>, y^(30)(2)_>) where y^(30)NF_> is a D-NF-bridge and y^(30)(2)_> is a D-(2)-bridge, together with isomorphisms to the model D~ and D^> so that conjugation sends one bridge to the other; isomorphisms of such Hodge theatres are pairs of isomorphisms of the constituent bridges inducing same bijection on index sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compositions likewise defined; these base Hodge theatres serve as the D-level skeletons prior to adding Frobenioid (F-) data to form full (2)-Hodge theatres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport of Label Classes via Base-Bridges (Proposition 10.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-(2)-Hodge theatre yHT_D-(2) with capsule yDJ and bridge y^(30)(2)_>, (1) the D-(2)-bridge structure at v in V_bad determines a bijection y^(31): J -> F_l; (2) for each j in J there are induced natural isomorphisms between LabCusp(yD^) and LabCusp(yD_j) as F_l-torsors constructed from the various v-portions of the bridge; (3) composing these yields a distinguished element [y^(15)] in LabCusp(yD~) and an isomorphism LabCusp(yD~) -> J ≃ F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic/group-theoretic descriptions produce these isomorphisms; compatibility with canonical elements is emphasised. The proposition underlies the process by which capsule-index sets and cusp-labels are synchronised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark on synchronisation indeterminacies (Remark 10.19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reconstructing maps (pi_1)-maps up to conjugacy, cuspidal inertia subgroups are likewise only defined up to conjugacy; there is no natural global synchronisation. However, by factoring certain open subgroups of index l (via Theorem 6.11) one can partially synchronise these indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remark is a cautionary note: algorithms produce objects up to conjugacy (inner ambiguity), and one must account for and sometimes factorise these ambiguities when composing local reconstructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of D-NF-Bridges, D-(2)-Bridges, D-(2)-Hodge theatres (Proposition 10.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated properties: (1) Isom(y^(30)NF_>, z^(30)NF_>) is an F_l-torsor; (2) For D-(2)-bridges Isom sets have cardinality 1; (3) For D-(2)-Hodge theatres Isom sets size 1; (4) Given a D-NF-bridge and a D-(2)-bridge the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms making them into a D-(2)-Hodge theatre is an F_l-torsor; (5) From a D-NF-bridge one has a functorial algorithm to construct a D-(2)-Hodge theatre up to F_l-indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural properties control automorphism/indeterminacy behaviour: NF-bridges have F_l-torsor families of isomorphisms, whereas (2)-bridges/Hodge theatres are rigid (unique isomorphism). The algorithmic construction note emphasises computability up to torsor ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-(2)-link (Definition 10.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(or D-)(2)NF-link (or D-(2)-link) between two D-(2)-Hodge theatres is the full poly-isomorphism between the mono-analyticisations of the codomains of the D-(2)-bridges: yD^' -> zD^'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark clarifies that in such a link the D'-prime-strips are shared but arithmetically-holomorphic structures are not; the 'étale-picture' diagram visualises shared/non-shared components and permutation symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local F-prime-strip construction and (label)-valuations (Definition 10.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) For (label) in LabCusp(yD~) a (label)-valuation in V(yD~) is a valuation lying in the image via the NF-bridge bijection of the unique D-prime-strip yD_j whose capsule contains that label; (2) Localising at each such valuation from yF~ (or related objects) one constructs an F-prime-strip yF_{j(label)} well-defined up to isomorphism; (3) A poly-morphism zF -> yF~ lying over an induced poly-morphism at D-level is compatible with local and global 1-coric structures; (4) For a capsule EF of F-prime-strips and an F-prime-strip yF one can define poly-morphisms EF -> yF~ (resp. EF -> yF) lying over induced poly-morphisms ED -> yD~ (resp. ED -> yF~).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because certain natural projections are non-injective, local F-prime-strips are only determined up to isomorphism; compatibility conditions with Kummer classes and pseudo-monoid poly-morphisms are required. These local constructions underpin model NF/(2)-bridges at the F-level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model (2)-Bridge and Model NF-Bridge; diagonal F-objects and localisation functors (Definition 10.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) For j in J the model (2)-bridge y^(2)_j : yF_j -> yF^> is the poly-morphism uniquely determined by the model D-(2)-bridge portion; (2) The model NF-bridge y^NF_j : yF_j -> yF~ is determined similarly; (3) One forms diagonal F-prime-strips yF_{hJ} by arranging copies of yF^> along diagonal subsets determined by bijections V_{hJ} -> V and obtains restriction/localisation functors gl: to loc:() -> yF_{vhJ} (and realisations yF~^R etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition ties the model D-structures to canonical F-level poly-morphisms and explains how diagonal constructions and localisation functors produce the multiple realisations and restriction maps needed for assembling global F-objects from local pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: NF-Bridge, (2)-Bridge, (2)-Hodge theatre (full definitions) (Definition 10.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) An NF-bridge is a collection (zFJ, z^NF_>, zF~, 99K) satisfying: capsule zFJ indexed by J, pre-Frobenioids zF~, zF~ isomorphic to model objects, an abstractly equivalent morphism zD~ -> zD^~ and isomorphism zF~ ≃ zF~|_{zD~}, and a poly-morphism z^NF_> lifting the D-NF-bridge; (2) A (2)-bridge is a collection (zFJ, z^(2)_>, zF^>, 99K, zHT(2)) analogously tying F-prime-strips to a (2)-Hodge theatre; (3) A (2)-Hodge theatre is an NF-bridge and a (2)-bridge whose associated D-level bridges form a D-(2)-Hodge theatre. Isomorphisms of these objects are triples/pairs of compatible poly-isomorphisms and Hodge theatre isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful compatibility conditions are required between the F-level and D-level data (99K links). One may associate D-level bridges to any NF-/ (2)-bridge and vice versa; these definitions formalise the full F- and D-level bridge apparatus used to build Hodge theatres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism and torsor properties of NF-bridges and (2)-bridges (Lemma 10.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) For NF-bridges/(2)-bridges/(2)-Hodge theatres whose associated D-bridges are given, the natural map from Isom at F-level to Isom at D-level is bijective. (2) For an NF-bridge z^NF_> and a (2)-bridge z^(2)_> the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms making them into a (2)-Hodge theatre is an F_l-torsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma ties F-level rigidity/indeterminacy to the D-level properties: isomorphisms are controlled by the D-level, and formation of a mixed Hodge theatre from NF and (2)-bridges has F_l-torsor ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive symmetry: F_l-group and F_l-torsor, Aut+ definitions (Definition 10.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: An F_l-group is a set E with an {±1}-orbit of bijections E -> Fl; an F_l-torsor is a set T with an F_l-orbit of bijections T -> Fl. For a chosen bijection f: T -> Fl in the orbit one obtains subgroups Aut+(T) and Aut^(-)(T) of Aut(Sets)(T) corresponding to positive and signed automorphisms; Aut+(T) is the subgroup of positive automorphisms and has a natural F_l-group structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements are called positive if sent to +1 by the natural surjection Aut(T) -> {±1}. The subgroup Aut+(T) is independent of the choice of f in its orbit; it and its complement control sign behavior at the torsor level and are used to define 'positive' vs 'negative' full poly-isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive counterpart LabCusp^(6) and Aut+(yDv) (Definition 10.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) From (pi_1)(yDv) one can reconstruct tempered/profinite groups corresponding to X_v; define yD^(6) = {yD^(6)_v}_{v in V}. (2) A (6)-label class of cusps LabCusp^(6)(yDv) is defined analogously and has an F_l-group structure; there exists a canonical zero element y^(17)_v^0 and a canonical element y^(17)^(6)_v well-defined up to multiplication by ±1. (3) The natural surjection Aut(yDv) -> {±1} coming from action on LabCusp^(6)(yDv) defines Aut+(yDv) as its kernel and Aut^(11)(yD) (for sign vectors) accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition parallels earlier LabCusp notions but in the additive (6)-variant; the Aut+ groups partition automorphisms into 'positive' (kernel) and 'signed/negative' parts and provide the sign-symmetry needed for +-full poly-isomorphism definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: +-full poly-isomorphisms and signed/positive labelling (Definition 10.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: A +-full poly-isomorphism yDv -> zDv (or between capsules) is a poly-isomorphism obtained as the Aut+(yDv)-orbit (resp. Aut+(yD)-orbit) of an isomorphism. If yD = zD there are precisely two +-full poly-isomorphisms yDv -> yDv, naturally bijecting with {±1}^V. The one determined by the identity automorphism is called positive; the other negative. Signed +-full poly-isomorphisms correspond to sign vectors in {±1}^V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concept fixes a notion of positivity/negativity for poly-isomorphisms relative to the Aut+ subgroup; capsule-level +-full poly-morphisms are collections of such local +-full poly-isomorphisms compatible with injections of index sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction to GL2(Fl)/{±1} image (Definition 10.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the model global object D~ one can group-theoretically construct the outer homomorphism Aut(X_K) = Aut(D~) -> GL2(Fl)/{±1} determined by EF[l] and the Galois action on (pi_1)^ab_X; the image contains the Borel subgroup of SL2(Fl)/{±1} because the covering XK -> X corresponds to the rank-one quotient of the abelianised fundamental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation identifies how arithmetic Galois images appear in the automorphism groups of the model object and motivates identifications used in the Model D-NF-Bridge definition: images like Im(GFmod) inside GL2(Fl)/{±1} play a role in defining V_un, VBor and related orbits.
